novelty_flags.label: Theorem iv-residual-forest / related_work
novelty_flags.one_line: Add Kawakami (2021), which directly studies IV-plus-proxy identification of joint potential outcomes and is a closer no-selection comparator for the residual-forest design than the current survey acknowledges.

source_verification_receipts.locator: PDF pp. 3–5, Section 3.1 Theorem 1 and Conditions 1–3; Section 3.2 Corollary 1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 1 identifies PN and PS under the displayed selected-data factorization, positive conditional cells, invertible Q matrices, and determinant-ratio inequalities; Corollary 1 gives the IV-plus-proxy extension under its factorization and Conditions 2–3.

source_verification_receipts.locator: PDF p. 12290, Theorem 1 and Conditions (1)–(3); pp. 12290–12291, equations (8)–(11) and Theorem 2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 1 identifies all four potential-outcome-type probabilities with positive conditional tables, W independent of Z given U, randomized treatment, invertible matrices, and determinant-ratio inequalities; the paper gives plug-in estimators and asymptotic normality.
The paper studies IV-based identification using covariate/proxy information and identifies joint probabilities of potential outcomes under conditions distinct from the selected-data model.
The paper studies identification and regular root-n inference for linear counterfactual targets when proximal bridge solutions are nonunique.
The paper develops e-variable based exact anytime-valid confidence sequences for contingency-table effect parameters.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add Kawakami (2021) to related work and state a theorem-level no-selection comparison: identify precisely which regular IV-plus-proxy conditions it covers and exhibit a selected or boundary response-cycle law outside it.
Make the field kernel narrower and more falsifiable by elevating one explicit nondegenerate boundary family into a standalone strict-separation corollary against the 2026 regular conditions.

For a stronger future tier, derive a computable equivalence/non-equivalence frontier against two named proxy identification procedures rather than positioning the atlas only as a boundary-complete classifier.

recommended_next_step: Revise the IV-plus-proxy literature comparison to include Kawakami (2021) and a strict scope-separation statement, then advance the field-tier atlas kernel to Stage 0.
